## Column {width=20%}

:::{.card .flow}
To inspect the tradeoffs between recall and throughput, select a dataset and a value of $k$.
Then, using the legend below, select the algorithms you are interested in.
:::

```{ojs}
//| output: false
db = DuckDBClient.of({
	summary: FileAttachment("results/summary.parquet"),
  algorithm_basics: {file: FileAttachment("algorithms_basics.csv"), header: true}
});
alldata = db.sql`select * from summary;`
algorithms = db.sql`
	select distinct algorithm
	from summary natural left join algorithm_basics
	where coalesce(is_gpu, false) = ${gpu_algorithms}
	order by all;
`
datasets = db.sql`
	select distinct dataset
	from summary
	where dataset not like '%-id-%'
	order by dataset;
`

palette = Array.from(d3["schemeTableau10"]);
ncolors = palette.length;
```

```{ojs}
//|output: false
// This is a bit cumbersome, but this is the way to have a reactive variable
// that triggers the re-evaluation of the dependent cells:
//
//  - https://observablehq.com/framework/reactivity#mutables
//  - https://observablehq.com/@dralletje/mutable
mutable_non_gpu_color_map = new Mutable(new Map([
	["lorann", palette[0]],
	["glass", palette[1]],
	["symphonyqg", palette[2]],
]));
non_gpu_color_map = mutable_non_gpu_color_map.generator

mutable_gpu_color_map = new Mutable(new Map([
	["cuvs-cagra", palette[0]],
	["faiss-gpu-ivf", palette[1]],
	["ggnn", palette[2]],
]));
gpu_color_map = mutable_gpu_color_map.generator

color_map = gpu_algorithms ? gpu_color_map : non_gpu_color_map
```

```{ojs}
//| fill: false
//| width: 20%
viewof selected_dataset = Inputs.select(
	datasets.map(d => d.dataset),
	{value: "landmark-nomic-768-normalized", label: "select dataset"}
);
k_values = db.sql`select distinct k from summary;`
viewof k_value = Inputs.select(k_values.map(d => d.k), {value: 10, label: "value of k"});
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false

d3.select("#legend")
	.selectAll("div")
	.data(algorithms)
	.join("div")
	.style("border-bottom", d => `solid 6px ${(color_map.has(d.algorithm))? color_map.get(d.algorithm) : "lightgray"}`)
	.style("border-top", "solid 1px lightgray")
	.style("border-left", "solid 1px lightgray")
	.style("border-right", "solid 1px lightgray")
	.style("border-radius", "4px")
	.style("padding-right", "5pt")
	.style("padding-left", "5pt")
	.on("click", (event, d)=> {
		const key = d.algorithm;
		let cm = new Map(color_map);
		console.log("Algorithm " + key);
		if (cm.has(key)) {
			cm.delete(key);
		} else {
			const usedColors = new Set(cm.values());
			const color = palette.find(color => !usedColors.has(color));
			if (color !== undefined) {
				cm.set(key, color);
			}
		}
		if (gpu_algorithms) {
			mutable_gpu_color_map.value = cm;
		} else {
			mutable_non_gpu_color_map.value = cm;
		}
		console.log(color_map);
		console.log(event.target);
	})
	.text(d => d.algorithm);
```

```{ojs}
//| title: Algorithm type
//| fill: false
viewof gpu_algorithms = {
	const control = html`
		<div class="form-check form-switch d-flex align-items-center gap-2">
			<input class="form-check-input mt-0" type="checkbox" role="switch" id="gpu-algorithms-toggle">
			<label class="form-check-label" for="gpu-algorithms-toggle">GPU algorithms</label>
		</div>
	`;
	const toggle = control.querySelector("input");
	Object.defineProperty(control, "value", {get: () => toggle.checked});
	return control;
}
```

## Column

### Row

```{ojs}
//| output: false
pareto = db.sql`WITH
filtered_summary AS (
	SELECT *
	FROM summary natural left join algorithm_basics
	WHERE coalesce(is_gpu, false) = ${gpu_algorithms}
),
ranked_points AS (
	SELECT
		algorithm, dataset, params, qps, recall, build_time, index_size,
		ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY algorithm, dataset ORDER BY qps) AS rank_qps,
		ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY algorithm, dataset ORDER BY recall) AS rank_recall
	FROM filtered_summary
	where dataset = ${selected_dataset} and k = ${k_value}
),
non_dominated AS (
	SELECT
		r1.algorithm, r1.dataset, r1.params, r1.qps, r1.recall,
		r1.build_time, r1.index_size
	FROM ranked_points r1
	LEFT JOIN ranked_points r2
	ON r1.algorithm = r2.algorithm
	AND r1.dataset = r2.dataset
	AND ((r1.rank_qps < r2.rank_qps AND r1.rank_recall <= r2.rank_recall) OR
		 (r1.rank_qps <= r2.rank_qps AND r1.rank_recall < r2.rank_recall))
	WHERE r2.recall IS NULL -- no dominating point
)
SELECT * FROM non_dominated;
`
highlighted = pareto.filter(d => color_map.has(d.algorithm));
background = pareto.filter(d => !color_map.has(d.algorithm));
```

```{ojs}
//| height: 100%
//| title: "Tradeoff between quality (recall) and efficiency (queries per second)"
viewof paretoplot = Plot.plot({
	style: {fontSize: "10pt"},
  x: {domain: [0, 1], grid: true},
  y: {type: "log", grid: true},
  marks: [
		Plot.ruleY([1]),
		Plot.ruleX([0]),
		Plot.line(background, {
			  x: "recall",
			  y: "qps",
			  stroke: "lightgray",
			  z: "algorithm",
			  marker: "circle-stroke",
			  tip: false
	    }),
		Plot.line(highlighted, {
			  x: "recall",
			  y: "qps",
			  stroke: (d) => color_map.get(d.algorithm),
			  z: "algorithm",
			  marker: "circle-stroke",
			  tip: false
	    }),
	  Plot.dot(highlighted, {
			  x: "recall",
			  y: "qps",
			  r: 4,
			  fill: (d) => color_map.get(d.algorithm),
			  stroke: "white",
			  strokeWidth: 0.5,
			  title: (d) => `${d.algorithm}\nrecall ${d.recall.toFixed(4)}\n` +
					`${d3.format(".3s")(d.qps)} qps\n` +
					`build ${d3.format(".3s")(d.build_time)} s\n` +
					`index ${d3.format(".3s")(d.index_size * 1024)}B`
	    }),
	  Plot.ruleX(background, Plot.pointerX({x: "recall", py: "qps", stroke: "red"}))
  ]
})
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
dynamic_recall_threshold = (paretoplot)? paretoplot.recall : null;
rankdata = db.sql`
	SELECT dataset, algorithm, k, max(qps) as qps,
		arg_max(build_time, qps) as build_time,
		arg_max(index_size, qps) as index_size,
		min(build_time) as cheapest_build
	FROM summary natural left join algorithm_basics
	WHERE recall > ${dynamic_recall_threshold}
	AND dataset = ${selected_dataset}
	AND coalesce(is_gpu, false) = ${gpu_algorithms}
	GROUP BY dataset, algorithm, k
`
half = d3.max(rankdata, d => d.qps) / 2
console.log(half)
```

```{ojs}
//| title: Ranking at the selected threshold, and what each configuration costs
// Three aligned charts sharing one row order: throughput ranks the algorithms,
// the other two say what that rank costs to build and to keep in memory. Separate
// panels rather than one plot, because the three quantities have different units.
{
  const rows = Array.from(rankdata);
  const order = rows.slice().sort((a, b) => b.qps - a.qps).map(d => d.algorithm);
  const height = 24 * order.length + 52;
  const fill = (d) => color_map.has(d.algorithm) ? color_map.get(d.algorithm) : "gray";
  const f = d3.format(".3s");
  const decade = (v) => Math.abs(Math.log10(v) - Math.round(Math.log10(v))) < 1e-6 ? f(v) : "";
  // seconds read badly in SI ("3.49ks"), so build times get human units
  const secs = (s) => s < 90 ? (s < 10 ? s.toFixed(1) : d3.format(".3r")(s)) + " s"
                    : s < 5400 ? (s / 60).toFixed(0) + " min"
                    : (s / 3600).toFixed(1) + " h";

  const throughput = Plot.plot({
    style: {fontSize: "11pt"},
    width: 430, height,
    marginLeft: 175, marginRight: 66, marginTop: 26, marginBottom: 34,
    x: {grid: true, label: "queries per second →"},
    y: {domain: order, label: null},
    marks: [
      Plot.ruleX([0]),
      Plot.barX(rows, {y: "algorithm", x: "qps", fill, inset: 1}),
      Plot.text(rows, {y: "algorithm", x: "qps", text: d => f(d.qps), dx: 7, textAnchor: "start"})
    ]
  });

  const minBuild = d3.min(rows, d => d.build_time);
  const minSize = d3.min(rows, d => d.index_size);
  const cells = rows.flatMap(d => [
    {algorithm: d.algorithm, metric: "build time", ratio: d.build_time / minBuild,
     label: secs(d.build_time),
     tip: `${d.algorithm}\nbuild ${secs(d.build_time)} — ${(d.build_time / minBuild).toFixed(1)}× the cheapest here` +
          `\ncheapest build clearing the threshold: ${secs(d.cheapest_build)}`},
    {algorithm: d.algorithm, metric: "index size", ratio: d.index_size / minSize,
     label: f(d.index_size * 1024) + "B",
     tip: `${d.algorithm}\nindex ${f(d.index_size * 1024)}B — ${(d.index_size / minSize).toFixed(1)}× the smallest here`}
  ]);
  const maxRatio = d3.max(cells, d => d.ratio);

  const resources = Plot.plot({
    style: {fontSize: "11pt"},
    width: 300, height,
    marginLeft: 10, marginRight: 10, marginTop: 26, marginBottom: 34,
    x: {domain: ["build time", "index size"], label: null, axis: "top"},
    y: {domain: order, axis: null},
    color: {type: "log", scheme: "blues", domain: [1, maxRatio]},
    marks: [
      Plot.cell(cells, {x: "metric", y: "algorithm", fill: "ratio", inset: 0.5, title: "tip"}),
      Plot.text(cells, {x: "metric", y: "algorithm", text: "label", fontSize: 10,
        fill: d => d.ratio > Math.sqrt(maxRatio) ? "white" : "black"})
    ]
  });

  const scale = Plot.legend({
    color: {type: "log", scheme: "blues", domain: [1, maxRatio],
            label: "× the cheapest build / smallest index on this dataset"},
    width: 300, style: {fontSize: "10pt"}
  });

  return html`<div>
    <div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 2px; align-items: flex-start;">
      ${throughput}${resources}
    </div>
    <div style="margin-top: 0.2rem;">${scale}</div>
    <div style="font-size: 0.8rem; color: #5a6570; margin-top: 0.3rem;">
      Throughput ranks the algorithms; the two cells say what that rank costs. Both are
      shaded by how many times they exceed the cheapest build and the smallest index on
      this dataset, so a dark row is expensive whichever way you read it. Hover a cell for
      the ratio, and for the cheapest build that still clears the same recall threshold.
    </div>
  </div>`;
}
```
